areas: Fort Ethan Allen Parade Grounds and Park
places: Church Street Marketplace
Four blocks of Church Street, car-free and paved in brick since 1981. Buskers in summer, holiday lights in winter, and the place everyone ends up.
Ben & Jerry's first scoop shop
Ben Cohen and Jerry Greenfield opened their first ice cream shop on this corner in 1978, in an old gas station. The building is gone; a plaque marks the spot.
City Hall Park
Downtown's town green, in front of City Hall. Its fountain, lawn and benches fill up on the first warm day of spring.
The Flynn
An Art Deco movie palace from 1930, now Burlington's main stage for concerts, comedy and the jazz festival.
Battery Park
Named for the gun battery that fired on British ships in the War of 1812. Today it is where people go to watch the sun set behind the Adirondacks.
Waterfront and the bike path
The bike path runs along the lake from Oakledge to the Winooski River and on across the Colchester causeway, where a little bike ferry crosses the gap in summer.
ECHO
The science centre and aquarium for Lake Champlain, right on the water.
Ferry to Port Kent
In summer, the ferry from the King Street dock crosses Lake Champlain to Port Kent, New York, in about an hour.
Union Station
The 1916 station at the bottom of Main Street. Passenger trains came back in 2022, when Amtrak's Ethan Allen Express started running to New York City.
The breakwater lights
Two small lighthouses mark the ends of the breakwater that shelters the harbour.
UVM and Ira Allen Chapel
The University of Vermont was chartered in 1791. The chapel's tower, named for founder Ira Allen, is the landmark you see on the hill from the lake.
Pine Street and the South End
Old industrial buildings full of studios, breweries and makers. Every September the South End Art Hop opens them all up.
Oakledge Park
Rocky shoreline, swimming coves, and a treehouse built so wheelchairs can roll right up into it.
North Beach
The city's long sandy beach, with a campground in the pines behind it.
The Intervale
Farmland on the Winooski River's floodplain, a few minutes' bike ride from downtown. Working farms, community gardens and trails, all within the city.
Ethan Allen Homestead
The 1787 farmhouse where Ethan Allen, leader of the Green Mountain Boys, spent his last years.
Winooski Falls and the mills
The river drops over these falls, which once powered Winooski's big woollen mills. The mills are now shops, offices and apartments.
The Winooski roundabout
Downtown Winooski wraps around one big roundabout, with restaurants on every side of it.
Red Rocks Park
South Burlington's lakeside woods, with trails along reddish rock cliffs above the water.
Burlington airport
BTV, in South Burlington. Also home to the Vermont Air National Guard's F-35s, which you will hear before you see.
